headline: S. 140 would have reauthorized Coast Guard funding, personnel levels, and maritime safety and shipping rules, but the Senate refused to take it up on April 18, 2018.
what_it_does: If adopted, this bill would have reorganized the Coast Guard's authorizing law and extended its programs and spending limits through fiscal years 2018 and 2019. It would have set personnel strength levels, authorized specific ship, aircraft, and facility purchases, and changed many rules on boat safety, recreational vessel equipment, fishing vessels, and ocean shipping. It would also have added a Vessel Incidental Discharge Act requiring national standards for ballast water and other ship discharges, and extended the Federal Maritime Commission.

who_it_affects.how: They would have had set end-of-year active duty strength targets, new parental leave rules, and changes to how retirement and promotion timing is figured.
They would have faced new engine cut-off switch requirements for certain small boats and five-year endorsements on some vessel certificates, with a fee for recreational vessel certificates.

who_it_affects.group: Commercial fishing vessel owners and crews
who_it_affects.how: They would have received exemptions from some survival craft rules and a new deadline and expanded length limit for the alternate safety compliance program.

who_it_affects.group: Ocean shipping companies and marine terminal operators
who_it_affects.how: They would have been barred from negotiating as a group for certain port and towing services and required to meet new FMC licensing and financial responsibility rules.

who_it_affects.group: Commercial vessel operators discharging ballast water
who_it_affects.how: They would have had to meet new national discharge standards set by NOAA, with several vessel types exempted.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of Crane Lake, Minnesota, and operators of passenger vessels there
who_it_affects.how: They would have been allowed to carry up to 12 passengers on certain uninspected vessels.
They would have been allowed to use marine throw bags as lifesaving equipment and skip an extra throwable device on rafts 16 feet or longer.
